title: Tool Schema Design — Naming, Descriptions, Parameter Constraints

questions.question: An assistant has two lookups that both say 'look up people' and keeps calling the wrong one. What is the cheapest fix?
options: Use a bigger model that guesses better
Merge both lookups into one tool with more options
Remove both tools and answer from training data
Rewrite the descriptions so each states when to use it and when not to
questions.explanation: Ambiguous descriptions force the model to guess. This lesson teaches the description pattern and atomic-tool split that make selection reliable.

questions.question: What warning does lint_name report for get_weather_in_tokyo?
options: A missing lowercase letter error
An embedded argument warning
A forbidden enum warning
No finding, because every snake_case name is ideal
questions.explanation: The name is syntactically snake_case, but the linter warns that a location has been embedded in the operation name.

questions.question: What happens when lint_description sees a hidden <system> instruction?
options: It adds a helpful-use warning and accepts the text
It only checks the description length
It blocks the description as an injection pattern
It changes the tool name to system
questions.explanation: Injection-like tags and instruction overrides are blocking findings in the description linter.

questions.question: What constraint does the GOOD_REGISTRY notes_search limit schema express?
options: A string with no bounds
A boolean that defaults to false
An arbitrary object whose keys are ignored
integer 1..50
questions.explanation: The search limit is an integer with minimum 1 and maximum 50, making the pagination contract explicit.

questions.question: Which finding is caused by the duplicate notes_list entries in BAD_REGISTRY?
options: A blocking duplicate-name finding
A harmless style nit about long words
A currency enum warning
A prompt-sampling capability error
questions.explanation: lint_registry requires unique names and blocks the registry when a name appears more than once.

questions.question: Why does the linter flag a monolithic action enum with more than three values?
options: Enums are never valid in JSON Schema
A large action switch hides multiple tools and weakens routing clarity
The linter cannot parse strings
Only numeric parameters may be required
questions.explanation: The action heuristic encourages separate, focused operations instead of one tool that bundles many unrelated modes.
